title: Phenome- and laboratory-wide meta-analyses of sickle cell trait reveal multi-system disease associations.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC full text returned HTTP 500, the supplementaryFiles endpoint returned a 297-byte non-zip response, there are no GEO/SRA/dbGaP links, and the Zenodo/Dryad DOI search found nothing. The only text-mined accessions are the variant IDs rs334, rs33930165 and rs34598529.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract only: 4,813 sickle cell trait carriers among 58,830 African-ancestry participants in three electronic health record biobanks (BioVU, Penn Medicine Biobank, All of Us), analysed with PheWAS (phenome-wide association) and LabWAS (lab-test-wide association), with replication in the Million Veteran Program.

a1_downloadable.note: Participant-level health record data from BioVU, Penn Medicine Biobank and All of Us is controlled access and needs an institutional application or a registered workbench. No open data deposit was found; this rests on the abstract plus failed repository and supplement lookups.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Only per-phenotype association summary statistics could be public (not verified). That is a few hundred effect sizes, not a labelled per-person table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked: no files were accessible.

a4_units_stated.note: Not checked: no files were accessible.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not checked: no files were accessible. Summary tables would have only hundreds of rows, one per phenotype.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not checked; summary tables would be small.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checked: no files were accessible.

a8_label_provenance.note: Diagnosis and lab codes come from health records, not from a model; but they cannot be accessed.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible without access to the participant-level health records, which need a controlled-access application.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use carrier status and health-record diagnoses and lab values to predict which sickle cell trait carriers develop kidney disease or blood clots.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-person diagnosis codes and lab results for about 58,830 African-ancestry biobank participants (figure from the abstract only; the data is not openly accessible).
plain_idea.predict: Later diagnoses such as kidney disease, taken from billing codes in the health records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinicians could flag high-risk carriers for screening. This is blocked by controlled access.

label_elsewhere.why: Not assessed because the data is controlled access.

ml_idea: Predict outcomes among sickle cell trait carriers from health-record data. This is infeasible without controlled-access biobank approval.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; the data is inaccessible.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the supplement has open per-phenotype summary statistics. Even if it does, there are only hundreds of rows and no per-person labels.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: the participant-level health records (BioVU, Penn Medicine Biobank, All of Us) are controlled access, and no open deposit or supplement could be retrieved. Any public output would be association summary statistics, not an ML-ready labelled table.
